title: Homological component criterion for the scalar second-projection splitting
statement: In the setting of [lem-sfb-rational-p1-scalar-p2-splitting], let U be the degree-zero unit on the projective line, V the shifted scalar line, K the second-projection direct image of the shifted scalar line, and let u2 and c2 be the explicit scalar twisted unit and transported P2 Chern adjunct. Then U is homologically concentrated in degree 0, V in degree -2, K in degrees 0 and -2, and the degree-zero map induced by c2 and degree-minus-two map induced by u2 are isomorphisms.

source.place: Second identity, scalar trace base change before tensoring with q*K

proof.text: The fully proved normalized completed-Chern splitting supplies a first completed-line arrow v for which biprod.desc v b is invertible. Its construction uses the given tower Result and the completed normalization of b.

Apply the given exact completed realization and the integral, rational and, when needed, algebraic-closure scalar functors. The endpoint isomorphisms, direct-image mates and final native-pushforward comparison preserve biproduct splittings. By definition the second arrow is scalarP2Chern. This constructs a first arrow v with biprod.desc v c2 invertible, without identifying v with the specified unit.

The degree-zero single unit is concentrated in degree zero and the shifted line in degree minus two. Additivity of homology and the splitting imply concentration of K in those two degrees, invertibility of H0(c2), and invertibility of Hminus2(v).

The diagonal is a section of the second projection. The composite pullback is isomorphic to the identity, so its adjunction unit is invertible and the second-projection unit is split mono. Its composite with the shifted-line comparison is therefore split mono, also after taking homology. Identify both Hminus2 source and target with the scalar line using Hminus2(v). The retraction is epic; on the common root cover both objects have rank-one bases, so the existing local rank-one epi criterion makes the retraction invertible. Local conservativity gives a global isomorphism, hence the specified Hminus2(u2) is invertible.

proof_origin.place: The normalized tower splitting transported to scalar coefficients; the specified unit is recovered in its nonzero homology degree by the diagonal section and the local rank-one epi criterion.
